_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for the Central African Republic covering Bantu and Sara peoples, Gbaya and Banda migrations, slave raiding zone, French Equatorial Africa (Ubangi-Shari), Bokassa's empire, coups and instability, Séléka/Anti-Balaka conflict, and Russian Wagner Group presence.

ethnic_groups.name: Gbaya
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; western CAR; led Kongo-Wara rebellion; slash-and-burn farmers

ethnic_groups.name: Banda
ethnic_groups.notes: Central and eastern CAR; diverse subgroups; severely impacted by slave raids

ethnic_groups.name: Sara
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern CAR; related to Sara of Chad; agriculturalists

ethnic_groups.name: Yakoma
ethnic_groups.notes: Southeastern CAR along Ubangi River; Kolingba's ethnic base

ethnic_groups.name: Zande/Nzakara
ethnic_groups.notes: Southeastern CAR; historically formed kingdoms; related to Zande in DRC and South Sudan

ethnic_groups.name: BaAka (Pygmy)
ethnic_groups.notes: Indigenous forest hunter-gatherers in southwestern rainforest; endangered culture

ethnic_groups.name: Fulani/Peul (Mbororo)
ethnic_groups.notes: Semi-nomadic cattle herders; caught in Séléka/Anti-Balaka conflict; Mbororo subgroup

ethnic_groups.name: Hausa/Arab traders
ethnic_groups.notes: Muslim trading communities in northern and eastern CAR

natural_resources.notes: Blood diamonds fund armed groups; uranium deposits (Bakouma, French interest); timber (tropical hardwoods, illegal logging); gold artisanal mining; 'paradox of plenty'—extraordinarily rich resources, poorest people; Bokassa's diamonds scandal with Giscard d'Estaing

military.notes: Army largely collapsed; MINUSCA (UN peacekeeping, ~14,000 troops) maintains fragile security; Russian Wagner Group/Africa Corps present (replaced French in influence); armed groups control ~80% of territory; Presidential Guard only reliable force

infrastructure.notes: Infrastructure destroyed by conflict; 2% paved roads.

debt_aid.notes: Among world's most aid-dependent; UN humanitarian appeals consistently; HIPC beneficiary; economy barely functions outside Bangui; barter economy in countryside

education.notes: Lowest education indicators globally; conflict shuttered most schools outside Bangui; 37% literacy (lowest in Africa); French-language instruction; armed groups recruit child soldiers

diaspora_migration.notes: Massive refugee production (745k external, 630k IDPs); Séléka/Anti-Balaka conflict 2013-present; Muslim minority fled to Chad/Cameroon; most displaced per capita in Africa

digital_economy.notes: Virtually no digital economy; among lowest internet penetration globally; Orange CAR primary telecom; Bitcoin legal tender (adopted 2022, largely symbolic, reversed); power outages constant; no tech ecosystem

country_profile.notes_unique: Rich in diamonds and gold yet one of the world's least developed countries; Jean-Bédel Bokassa crowned himself 'emperor' in a lavish 1977 ceremony.

geography.terrain: Vast flat to rolling plateau; scattered hills in northeast and southwest
geography.notes: Landlocked; dense rainforest in south, savanna in north; Dzanga-Sangha rainforest shelters forest elephants and lowland gorillas.

economy_extended.notes: One of the world's poorest nations despite mineral wealth (diamonds, gold, uranium); conflict devastates economy; subsistence agriculture; timber and diamonds main exports.

health.notes: Among world's worst health indicators; armed conflict destroyed health infrastructure; MSF and WHO primary providers in many areas.

food_agriculture.notes: Severe food insecurity due to conflict; 2.9M people need food assistance (2024); transhumance pastoralism; limited commercial farming.

energy.notes: One of world's lowest electrification rates; only Bangui has grid power; wood/charcoal 95% of energy; Boali hydropower dam.

transport.notes: Landlocked; Oubangui River to Congo/DRC only waterway; mostly unpaved roads; conflict makes many roads impassable.

unesco_sites_list: Manovo-Gounda St Floris National Park (in danger)
tourism.notes: Tourism near zero due to conflict; eco-tourism potential with gorilla tracking in Dzanga-Sangha.

human_rights_gender.notes: Severe abuses by armed groups (Anti-Balaka, ex-Séléka); conflict-related sexual violence; child soldiers; ICC investigations.

active_conflicts: Multi-sided civil war/instability (Anti-Balaka vs ex-Séléka factions)
security_stability.notes: MINUSCA (UN peacekeeping) with 15,000 troops; Russian Wagner Group presence; 2019 peace agreement partially holds; elections held but fragile.

intangible_heritage_items: Polyphonic singing of the Aka Pygmies (UNESCO)
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: Fragile; Radio Ndeke Luka main independent; MINUSCA radio; state media limited
cultural_heritage.notes: Aka Pygmy musical tradition is world-renowned; diverse ethnic groups (Gbaya, Banda, Mandja, Sara).

legal_system.notes: Special Criminal Court (SCC, est. 2015) for conflict crimes; ICC cases (Bemba, Said); justice system barely functions outside Bangui.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Consistently ranks near bottom on development and peace indices.

current_leader.name: Faustin-Archange Touadéra
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Former PM; elected post-Séléka crisis; re-elected 2020; relies on Russian Wagner Group support

former_leaders.name: Barthélemy Boganda
former_leaders.notes: Founding father; died in plane crash before independence; 'father of the nation'

former_leaders.name: David Dacko
former_leaders.notes: First president; Boganda's nephew; restored after Bokassa but overthrown again

former_leaders.name: Jean-Bédel Bokassa
former_leaders.notes: Self-proclaimed emperor; coronation 1977; overthrown by French Operation Barracuda

former_leaders.name: André Kolingba
former_leaders.notes: Military ruler; Yakoma ethnic base; forced into multiparty elections

former_leaders.name: Ange-Félix Patassé
former_leaders.notes: Elected president; faced army mutinies; overthrown by Bozizé

former_leaders.name: François Bozizé
former_leaders.notes: Military coup leader; overthrown by Séléka coalition

former_leaders.name: Michel Djotodia
former_leaders.notes: Séléka leader; first Muslim head of state; forced to resign under international pressure

former_leaders.name: Catherine Samba-Panza
former_leaders.notes: Transitional president; first female head of state of CAR
